lines.text: Wait you or wait for you?
Many learners say: I wait you at the door.
Better: I wait for you at the door.

data.wrong: I wait you at the door.
data.right: I wait for you at the door.

native.tip: Ждать — “wait for”: “I wait for you at the door”.
native.caption: Ты тоже говоришь “I wait you at the door.”? 😅 По-русски «жду тебя» — без предлога, а по-английски нужен “for”. Правильно: “I wait for you at the door.”. Послушай Ама и повтори! Больше практики — в приложении Lexkite.

en.hook: Wait you or wait for you?
en.tip: To wait is “wait for”: “I wait for you at the door”.
en.caption: Do you also say “I wait you at the door.”? 😅 In Russian “zhdu tebya” has no preposition, but English needs “for”. Correct: “I wait for you at the door.”. Listen to Ama and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.
